name: Boric acid

lead: Boric acid is a weak acid that has been used as a mild antiseptic for minor burns and cuts and, very dilute, as an eyewash. It is also used as an insecticide and in second-line vaginal treatment for resistant yeast infections.
For skin it is relevant as a topical antiseptic for minor irritations.

paras: It is sold as powder, dilute solution or dressings. Specific use instructions are not given here.

A 2021 toxicology review notes intact skin is a better barrier than damaged skin, that skin exposure has been fatal in some cases and that animal studies show reproductive toxicity [2]. Wikipedia reports that the EU classifies it as reprotoxic category 2 and that repeated use on abraded skin or as an eyewash is considered toxic, especially for infants [1].

chain: Calms minor skin irritation or eye surface
angle.text: As a mild antiseptic, boric acid has been used on minor skin and eye irritation. Its use is limited by toxicity at high exposure.

lead: Boric acid is a weak acid first prepared by Wilhelm Homberg from borax; it has been used for centuries in cleaning and preservation [1]. Medically it serves as a mild antiseptic for minor burns and cuts and, in very dilute form, an eyewash [1].

It is also an insecticide, registered in the US in 1948, and a second-line option for recurrent vaginal candidiasis; a 2011 review of 14 studies reported mycologic cure rates of 40% to 100% [1][2]. In 2008 the EU reclassified it as reprotoxic category 2 [1].

paras: Wikipedia lists antiseptic use on minor burns and cuts and as a dilute eyewash, with vaginal suppositories as second-line therapy and insecticide use [1].

A 2021 review describes boron absorption by mouth, a weaker skin barrier when skin is damaged, fatal cases after skin or oral exposure and reproductive toxicity in animals [3]. A case report describes boric acid poisoning [4].

A 2011 review identified 14 studies (2 randomised trials, 9 case series, 4 case reports) of intravaginal boric acid, with cure rates of 40% to 100% [2]. No studies were found on boric acid for cosmetic skin purposes.
